You are differential-testing a Rust port against its C++ reference.

  reference : /workspace/dataset/test15_executable
  port      : /output/test15

Both take the same argv. A case PASSES only if stdout bytes, stderr bytes AND exit status all match exactly.
Compare BYTES, not text: some outputs are deliberately invalid UTF-8, and one input class makes both programs abort.

There is a ready-made helper at /tmp/probe/difflib.sh:

    source /tmp/probe/difflib.sh
    diffcase arg1 arg2 ...      # runs both, records pass/fail
    report                      # prints "pass=N fail=M" plus failing details

Use it, or write your own comparator if you prefer — but it MUST compare stdout bytes, stderr bytes and exit code.
Beware: inputs whose first argument is empty, or ends with ':', make BOTH binaries abort with SIGABRT (exit 134) and
print a libstdc++ diagnostic to stderr. That is expected shared behaviour, not a divergence — the port reproduces it
deliberately. Only report a divergence when the two binaries DISAGREE.

The Rust source lives in /output (test15.rs, src/inflection/*.rs). You MAY read it to find weak spots to attack.
You may NOT modify it. Do not read or look for C++ library source; it does not exist on disk.

Known behaviour of the reference, for context (derived by earlier probing — treat as claims to attack, not gospel):
  pluralize(w)  = w if w is empty or one of {equipment,information,rice,money,species,series,fish,sheep,jeans,police}
                  (exact, case-sensitive, whole-string), else w + "s"
  camelize(w)   = drop '_' separators, ASCII-uppercase the byte after each run of them; first byte untouched
                  unless the input starts with '_'
  underscore(w) = for each byte: if ASCII uppercase, emit '_' (unless byte index 0) then the lowercase byte;
                  else emit the byte unchanged
  isPlural(w)   = false if w is uncountable (whole word) or ends with "news";
                  else true if w ends with one of s / ta / ia / mice / lice / octopi / viri, or w == "oxen"
  isSingular(w) = !isPlural(w)
  demodulize(p) = p[p.rfind(':') + 2 ..]  (aborts when that offset exceeds the length)
  driver: args 1..min(argc-1,5) each contribute pluralize+camelize, plus underscore when the index is even;
          all buffered and printed first, then isPlural/isSingular/demodulize of argv[1].

Run AT LEAST 3000 comparison cases. Report precisely.

=== YOUR STRATEGY: colons-and-abort ===
Strategy: attack demodulize, including the abort path.
Generate thousands of arguments built from ':' plus other bytes: every string of length 0-6 over { ':', 'a' }
(exhaustive, 127 strings), plus random strings with colons at random positions, plus colons combined with multi-byte
UTF-8, plus arguments that are only colons of every length 0-30.
CRITICAL: verify the abort cases match EXACTLY — same stderr bytes (including the two numbers in the
"__pos (which is N) > this->size() (which is M)" message), same exit status, and the SAME stdout produced before the
abort. Test the abort with 1..6 arguments so there is buffered stdout to flush first.
Also confirm which inputs abort and which do not, and that the two binaries agree on that partition for every case.
At least 3000 cases.

#!/bin/bash
# Differential tester: run the C++ reference and the Rust port with identical
# argv, compare stdout bytes, stderr bytes and exit status.
CPP=/workspace/dataset/test15_executable
RUST=${RUST_BIN:-/output/test15}
pass=0; fail=0
declare -a FAILURES

diffcase() {
  local co ce cx ro re rx
  co=$("$CPP" "$@" 2>/tmp/dt.ce | od -An -v -tx1 | tr -d ' \n'); cx=$?
  ce=$(od -An -v -tx1 < /tmp/dt.ce | tr -d ' \n')
  ro=$("$RUST" "$@" 2>/tmp/dt.re | od -An -v -tx1 | tr -d ' \n'); rx=$?
  re=$(od -An -v -tx1 < /tmp/dt.re | tr -d ' \n')
  if [ "$co" = "$ro" ] && [ "$ce" = "$re" ] && [ "$cx" = "$rx" ]; then
    pass=$((pass+1))
  else
    fail=$((fail+1))
    FAILURES+=("ARGS=$(printf '<%s> ' "$@")
   cpp: exit=$cx out=$co err=$ce
  rust: exit=$rx out=$ro err=$re")
  fi
}

report() {
  echo "pass=$pass fail=$fail"
  if [ "$fail" -gt 0 ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "${FAILURES[@]}" | head -100
    return 1
  fi
  return 0
}

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Byte-exact differential runner: stdout bytes, stderr bytes, exit status."""
import subprocess, sys, os, itertools, random, json

CPP = "/workspace/dataset/test15_executable"
RUST = "/output/test15"

npass = 0
fails = []
abort_cpp = set()
abort_rust = set()
cases = 0

def run(exe, args):
    p = subprocess.run([exe] + args, stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
                       stderr=subprocess.PIPE, close_fds=True)
    return p.stdout, p.stderr, p.returncode

def diffcase(args):
    global npass, cases
    cases += 1
    co, ce, cx = run(CPP, args)
    ro, re_, rx = run(RUST, args)
    # normalise signal death: python gives -6, shell gives 134
    cxn = 128 - cx if cx < 0 else cx
    rxn = 128 - rx if rx < 0 else rx
    cab = (cx == -6)
    rab = (rx == -6)
    key = tuple(args)
    if cab: abort_cpp.add(key)
    if rab: abort_rust.add(key)
    if co == ro and ce == re_ and cx == rx:
        npass += 1
        return True
    fails.append({
        "argv": [a.decode('utf-8', 'backslashreplace') if isinstance(a, bytes) else a for a in args],
        "argv_hex": [ (a.encode() if isinstance(a,str) else a).hex() for a in args],
        "cpp": {"exit": cx, "out": co.hex(), "err": ce.decode('utf-8','backslashreplace')},
        "rust": {"exit": rx, "out": ro.hex(), "err": re_.decode('utf-8','backslashreplace')},
    })
    return False

def expect_abort(args):
    """Model: abort iff argv[1] is empty or ends with ':' (argc>1)."""
    if len(args) < 1:
        return False
    a = args[0]
    return a == "" or a.endswith(":")

def report():
    print("pass=%d fail=%d" % (npass, len(fails)))
    print("cases=%d" % cases)
    print("abort_cpp=%d abort_rust=%d abort_agree=%s" % (
        len(abort_cpp), len(abort_rust), abort_cpp == abort_rust))
    if abort_cpp != abort_rust:
        print("ONLY_CPP:", list(abort_cpp - abort_rust)[:20])
        print("ONLY_RUST:", list(abort_rust - abort_cpp)[:20])
    # check partition against the model
    mism = []
    for key in set(list(abort_cpp) + list(abort_rust)):
        pass
    for f in fails[:40]:
        print(json.dumps(f, indent=1))
    return len(fails)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
import sys, os, random, itertools, json
sys.path.insert(0, "/tmp/probe")
import dt

def B(x):
    return x if isinstance(x, bytes) else x.encode()

def case(*args):
    dt.diffcase([B(a) for a in args])

random.seed(20260808)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- group 1
# Exhaustive: every string of length 0..6 over {':','a'}  -> 127 strings
alpha = [b':', b'a']
exhaustive = []
for n in range(0, 7):
    for tup in itertools.product(alpha, repeat=n):
        exhaustive.append(b"".join(tup))
assert len(exhaustive) == 127, len(exhaustive)

for s in exhaustive:
    case(s)                          # 1 arg
for s in exhaustive:
    case(s, b"x")                    # 2 args -> underscore too
for s in exhaustive:
    case(s, b"B_c", b"D:e")          # 3 args
for s in exhaustive:
    case(s, b"a:", b"", b"::")       # 4 args, later args also colon-y
for s in exhaustive:
    case(s, b"1", b"2", b"3", b"4")  # 5 args
for s in exhaustive:
    case(s, b"1", b"2", b"3", b"4", b"5", b"6")  # 7 args (>5 -> ignored tail)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- group 2
# Colon-only strings of every length 0..30, alone and with company
for n in range(0, 31):
    s = b":" * n
    case(s)
    case(s, b"pre")
    case(s, b"pre", b"mid")
    case(b"pre", s)
    case(b"pre", b"mid", s)
    case(s, s, s, s, s)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- group 3
# Exhaustive length 0..4 over {':','a','B','_'} = 1+4+16+64+256 = 341
alpha4 = [b':', b'a', b'B', b'_']
ex4 = []
for n in range(0, 5):
    for tup in itertools.product(alpha4, repeat=n):
        ex4.append(b"".join(tup))
assert len(ex4) == 341, len(ex4)
for s in ex4:
    case(s)
for s in ex4:
    case(s, b"Second_Arg:")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- group 4
# Colons combined with multi-byte UTF-8 / raw high bytes.
mb = ["é", "€", "𝄞", "漢字", "naïve", "Ünïcödé", "🎉", "ẞ", "Ā", "ÿ"]
raw = [b"\xc3", b"\xc3\xa9", b"\xe2\x82", b"\xf0\x9f\x8e", b"\xff\xfe", b"\x80\x80", b"\xed\xa0\x80"]
pieces = [B(x) for x in mb] + raw
for p in pieces:
    for pat in [b":%s", b"%s:", b"::%s", b"%s::", b":%s:", b"%s:%s" ]:
        try:
            s = pat % ((p,) * pat.count(b"%s"))
        except TypeError:
            continue
        case(s)
        case(s, b"tail")
        case(b"lead:", s)
    # colon inserted at every byte offset inside the multibyte sequence
    for i in range(len(p) + 1):
        s = p[:i] + b":" + p[i:]
        case(s)
        case(s, b"x", b"y")
        case(b"a", s)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- group 5
# Random strings with colons at random positions (bytes incl. non-UTF8).
pool = list(b"abcXYZ_0 .:/-") + [0xc3, 0xa9, 0xe2, 0x82, 0xac, 0xff, 0x7f, 0x01, 0x0a, 0x09]
for _ in range(900):
    n = random.randint(0, 12)
    s = bytes(random.choice(pool) for _ in range(n))
    # force some colons
    if n and random.random() < 0.7:
        s = bytearray(s)
        for _ in range(random.randint(1, 3)):
            s[random.randrange(n)] = 0x3a
        s = bytes(s)
    k = random.randint(1, 6)
    extra = []
    for _ in range(k - 1):
        m = random.randint(0, 6)
        e = bytes(random.choice(pool) for _ in range(m))
        extra.append(e)
    case(s, *extra)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- group 6
# Long strings / big offsets in the abort message.
for n in [7, 8, 9, 15, 16, 31, 32, 63, 64, 99, 100, 127, 128, 255, 256, 511,
          512, 999, 1000, 1023, 1024, 4095, 4096, 9999, 10000, 65535]:
    case(b"a" * n + b":")            # aborts, size = 8+n+1
    case(b"a" * n)                   # no abort
    case(b":" + b"a" * n)            # colon at front
    case(b"a" * n + b":" + b"b")     # colon then one byte -> empty result
    case(b"a" * n + b":", b"z")      # abort with buffered stdout

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- group 7
# Boundary: colon as second-to-last / last byte, all short lengths.
for n in range(0, 20):
    base = bytes(97 + (i % 26) for i in range(n))
    for pos in range(n + 1):
        s = base[:pos] + b":" + base[pos:]
        case(s)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- group 8
# Every single byte value 0x01..0xff as a 1-byte arg, and with a colon around.
for b in range(1, 256):
    ch = bytes([b])
    case(ch)
    case(b":" + ch)
    case(ch + b":")

print(dt.report())
